evals.name: Happy path: basic feature spec generation
evals.description: Given a simple feature request ('Add password reset via email'), the skill must produce a complete spec, plan, and task breakdown in a single output, with all three sections clearly delimited.
criteria: Output contains a 'Spec' section with purpose, functional requirements, and acceptance criteria
Output contains a 'Plan' section with architecture decisions, data model changes, or API contracts
Output contains a 'Task breakdown' section with ordered, self-contained tasks
Output contains at least one [ASSUMPTION: ...] marker
Output contains an assumptions summary section
evals.fail: Any of the 5 criteria is missing

evals.name: Non-functional requirements inclusion
evals.description: Given a feature request with implicit performance needs ('Build an admin dashboard showing daily active users'), the generated spec must include non-functional requirements covering performance, security, or storage.
evals.input: /spec-writer Build an admin dashboard showing daily active users
criteria: Spec section includes at least one non-functional requirement (performance, security, storage, latency, concurrency, or accessibility)
The non-functional requirement is stated explicitly (not embedded in a functional requirement)
Plan section addresses the non-functional constraint with a concrete decision
evals.fail: Any of the 3 criteria is missing

evals.name: Assumption marker correctness
evals.description: Every [ASSUMPTION] marker must include an impact rating (HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) and correction guidance explaining when the assumption should be revisited.
evals.input: /spec-writer Let users invite teammates to their workspace
criteria: Every [ASSUMPTION: ...] marker contains an explicit impact rating (HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW)
Every [ASSUMPTION: ...] marker includes correction guidance ('Correct this if: ...')
The assumptions summary at the end is sorted or grouped by impact level
Held assumptions are at least 2 in number
evals.fail: Any of the 4 criteria is missing — particularly if any assumption lacks an impact rating or correction guidance

evals.name: Edge-case coverage
evals.description: Given a feature request involving boundaries ('Add rate limiting to the public API'), the generated spec must cover edge cases including empty states, error states, boundary conditions, and concurrent access.
evals.input: /spec-writer Add rate limiting to the public API
criteria: Spec includes at least 3 distinct edge cases (empty state, error state, or boundary condition)
At least one edge case addresses concurrent access or race conditions
Acceptance criteria include at least one Given/When/Then that tests a boundary (e.g. 'Given the rate limit is N requests/minute, When the N+1th request arrives, Then the API returns 429')
evals.fail: Any of the 3 criteria is missing

evals.name: Spec/plan separation
evals.description: The Spec section must remain technology-agnostic. No framework, library, database, or infrastructure choice should appear in the Spec. Technology decisions belong only in the Plan section.
criteria: Spec section contains no mention of specific frameworks, libraries, databases, or infrastructure tools
Plan section contains at least one concrete technology decision (framework, library, database, or service)
Acceptance criteria in the Spec section do not reference implementation details
evals.fail: Any of the 3 criteria is missing (e.g. a framework name appears in an acceptance criterion, or the Plan contains no concrete decisions)
